messages.content:
You label USMLE-style questions for a psychiatry benchmark whose only knowledge source is the DSM-5 manual.

Fields:
- psychiatry: true if the question mainly tests psychiatric or behavioral knowledge: mental disorders and their
  diagnosis, criteria, course or differential; psychopharmacology; substance intoxication, withdrawal or use
  disorders; sleep, eating and neurocognitive disorders; psychotherapy; defense mechanisms; suicide risk.
  False when psychiatric words are incidental (e.g. "ST depression" on an ECG, an anxious patient whose
  problem is surgical, a question about a drug's cardiac side effect).
- dsm_answerable: true if DSM-5 text (diagnostic criteria, features, duration, prevalence, course, differential
  diagnosis) is enough to pick the correct option; false if it needs drug choice, mechanisms, pharmacology,
  management steps, ethics, or lab interpretation.
- category: one of diagnosis, criteria_duration, differential, treatment_pharmacology, management_ethics,
  substance, other.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"psychiatry": true or false, "dsm_answerable": true or false, "category": "...", "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
A 16-year-old African-American boy is brought to the physician because of a 2-month history of progressive right shoulder pain. He has had many episodes of joint and bone pain in the past, and as a child, had recurrent painful swelling of his hands and feet. His brother had a stroke at 6 years of age and now has an intellectual disability. The patient is at the 60th percentile for height and 55th percentile for weight. His vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows tenderness of the right anterior humerus without noticeable swelling or skin changes. Active and passive range of motion of the right shoulder is decreased and there is pain with movement. The leukocyte count is 4600/mm3. An x-ray of the right shoulder shows subchondral lucency of the humeral head with sclerosis and joint space narrowing. Which of the following is the most likely explanation for this patient's symptoms?

Options:
A. Infection of the dermis and subcutaneous tissue
B. Infection of the bone
C. Crystal deposition within the joint
D. Infarction of the bone trabeculae
E. Loss of bone mineral density

Correct answer: D. Infarction of the bone trabeculae

text: {"psychiatry": false, "dsm_answerable": false, "category": "other", "reason": "This is a hematology question about sickle cell disease causing avascular necrosis; the mention of intellectual disability is incidental and no psychiatric knowledge is tested."}
